Collecting trauma techniques is not the same as knowing how to formulate a trauma case.

A modality can provide powerful methods. It should not be required to do all of the clinical thinking for us.

When every presentation leads to the same intervention, when treatment becomes unclear after a client does not respond as expected, or when recommendations from different models conflict, the missing piece may be a broader clinical framework.

Foundations of Trauma Therapy is a two-day live virtual intensive focused on formulation, sequencing, readiness, relational context, and clinical decision-making across trauma modalities.

People often use the phrase "psychological evaluation" as though every evaluation is the same.

It is not.

The referral question determines what information needs to be gathered, which measures may be appropriate, who should contribute information, and what the final evaluation is expected to explain.

Our blog explains the differences among educational, psychological, neuropsychological, and neurodevelopmental evaluations-and why selecting the right type matters.

Parenting children and teens can involve moments of pride, uncertainty, conflict, connection, and constant adjustment.

Parenting With Purpose is a monthly virtual support group for adults who want to strengthen their parenting skills while connecting with others facing similar questions.

The first meeting will focus on understanding children's and teens' emotions. Participants will explore emotional cues, reflection questions, and practical ways to support emotional awareness at home.

Nature-informed work should not begin with the question, "What outdoor intervention could I add?"

It begins with clinical indication, accessibility, containment, ethics, and fidelity to the treatment model.

In the August 21 Nature-Based EMDR workshop, we will examine how clinicians can make those decisions thoughtfully within EMDR practice.

Parents are often expected to know how to respond to every emotional change, conflict, developmental shift, and difficult conversation.

Most people were never taught how.

Support does not mean someone else has the perfect answer. It means having a place to think, learn, ask questions, and feel less alone while developing skills that fit your family.

Parenting With Purpose begins August 21 and will meet virtually once a month.

CFBL Institute currently offers two live clinical trainings, but they are designed to answer different questions.

Nature-Based EMDR is for EMDR-trained clinicians who want to integrate nature intentionally while considering clinical indication, accessibility, ethics, and standard EMDR practice.

Foundations of Trauma Therapy is a two-day live virtual intensive for clinicians who want a stronger framework for formulation and treatment planning across trauma modalities.

Choose the training based on the clinical question you need answered.
